records.text: The owner decided on 26 October 2026 that sanctions aimed at a third country do not count as pressure on the listed firm's country (pressure-def-3.0), and that the questions issued with the record's start come from Polymarket and Kalshi markets on country pairs. The 24 forecasts of 26 October 2026 under pressure-def-2.1 are withdrawn and archived unchanged in forecasts/archive/2026-10-27-definition-2.1/. Nothing had been resolved or scored and no monthly cycle had been issued. This ledger starts here; nothing issued under it is ever edited or withdrawn.
records.title: Fresh start under pressure-def-3.0

records.author: model (automatic)

backtest.assumption: the pair's chance for the issue month held for 8 months
backtest.bootstrap: 10,000 resamples of runs of 8 consecutive issue months (windows that overlap are kept together)
backtest.outcome_rule: a measure dated in the window and recorded within 90 days after it closed (the live resolution's deadline)
backtest.persistence_rule: a measure by the pair known at the issue date in the 8 months before the window
backtest.windows_resolved_by: the window's own deadline at the issue date (window_due <= issue date)

information.derivation: 1 - (1 - monthly chance) ^ months covered: the pair's chance for the first full month of the window, from inputs known on the issue date, held for every month of the window (an assumption)

features_described.news_tension: Rise in the share of conflict in the news between A and B (GDELT): the last 3 months against the 2 years before
features_described.own_12m: Any measure by A against B in the last 12 months
features_described.own_count_36m: Months with a measure by A against B in the last 36 months (log)
features_described.own_fade_3m: Measures by A against B, fading with a 3-month half-life (log)
features_described.pair_tendency: How often A has taken measures against B over the whole record, shrunk towards what A's and B's tendencies imply (log-odds)

First, programme codes: listings under Sudan's and Tunisia's sanctions programmes (EU-SDNZ, SDNZ, CH-FIAA-TN and Japan's Darfur list) are now read as aimed at those countries, so they are third-country sanctions against anyone else, and the Hamas and Al-Shabaab regimes (EU-HAM, HAM, SECO-HAMAS, UN-SC2713) as counter-terrorism, which the definition leaves out. 12 positive pair-months of 2016-2026 are removed and none added (1,593 remain). Recomputed from the specification the questions were issued from, with and without this correction, the largest move of a chance is 0.1969 points (MKT:JPN>USA:2026-10-27). Second, recording cutoffs: an answer counts records first seen through its cutoff day, the whole day included, and is sealed only after that day. November 2026's preliminary reading counts records through 30 December and is sealed from 31 December; its mature answer counts records through 28 February 2027 and is sealed from 1 March. A question taken from a market counts records through the 90th day after its deadline day (31 March 2027 for a deadline of 31 December 2026) and is answered the next day; the code had also counted the 91st day. The back-test that calibrated these questions counted the 91st day too. Correcting it changes two 14-month window labels (RUS -> USA in the window from 2023-06, RUS -> CHN in the window from 2023-06) and none at 2, 5 or 8 months. The 14-month Brier score moves from 0.025496 to 0.025489, and the skill against persistence stays 20.35%. The chances stand as issued.

records.text: An independent review of 28 October 2026 found three things to correct in records 30 to 53, the short-deadline questions of that day, before any is answered. Their chances stand as issued. First, each record's back-test says its outcomes were recorded within 90 days; they were recorded within 30 days, the questions' own period. Second, those back-tests and the base rates and persistence beside them took a window as answered only once a 90-day answer would have been complete, so they end with windows starting in 2026-06 and 2026-05 where the 30-day answers allowed 2026-08 and 2026-07. Third, they are for whole calendar months (November 2026, or November and December), a proxy for each question's own window, which starts on 28 October and ends on its deadline day. This note gives each question's figures for its own window, computed the same way at every origin from what was known on that day: 4-day window to 2026-10-31 (5 questions): base rate 0.1%, back-test over 129 origins, errors 4.0% smaller than persistence (90% range 2.0% to 5.9%); 6-day window to 2026-11-02 (1 question): base rate 0.1%, back-test over 129 origins, errors 5.4% smaller than persistence (90% range 3.3% to 7.3%); 14-day window to 2026-11-10 (1 question): base rate 0.3%, back-test over 129 origins, errors 10.7% smaller than persistence (90% range 8.0% to 13.2%); 65-day window to 2026-12-31 (17 questions): base rate 1.0%, back-test over 127 origins, errors 21.4% smaller than persistence (90% range 19.4% to 23.1%).

rules.question: Will {A} take a new pressure measure against {B} in {month}?
counts: A trade measure: Global Trade Alert records a measure by {A}'s government (for the EU, one adopted at EU level) that it rates harmful, aimed explicitly at {B} (named among at most ten countries; GTA's 'targeted', not 'inferred'), of a kind a government can aim at another country: tariffs and other import charges; import or export bans, quotas and licensing; export controls; sanitary, technical and customs rules; financial, investment and payment restrictions; port and channel restrictions. A measure on named firms or people that its record says concerns a sanctioned third country (such as Russia or Iran) does not count against the other countries it names. Dated by its announcement (or, without one, its start).

Sanctions: {A}'s government adds at least one person, company or vessel connected to {B} to a sanctions or export-control list, under a programme aimed at {B} itself or a thematic one (human rights, corruption, military end users). Listings under a programme aimed at a third country (a firm in {B} listed for helping another country's government, such as Russia's or Iran's) do not count, nor do counter-terrorism, narcotics, organised crime and cyber-crime listings. Dated by listing.
A WTO dispute: {A} formally opens a dispute with {B} at the World Trade Organization (a request for consultations). Dated by the request.
not_counted: Trade remedies (anti-dumping, anti-subsidy and safeguard duties), subsidies and measures applying to all countries alike.
Renewals or extensions without change (they are not new records in these sources).
rules.resolution: Answered automatically from what Global Trade Alert, the sanctions lists and the WTO record by the 30th day after the month ends: yes if any measure above is dated in the month, otherwise no. This 30-day answer is the headline: the model is trained on 30-day answers, its back-test uses the same rule, and each month is judged on it first. A measure recorded later does not change a sealed answer. Global Trade Alert often records measures months after they are announced, so each month is checked again from what is recorded by the 90th day after it ends; the check lists any pair whose answer changed, so late records are shown, not hidden.
rules.pairs: Every direction between the 40 largest economies, Lithuania, Georgia and the EU, leaving out pairs inside the EU (members with each other, and the EU with a member).
rules.warning: An early warning means pressure is rising for the pair: this month's chance is at least twice its usual chance (the model's average for the pair over the previous 12 months) and at least 10%. Pairs that are always under pressure stay near their usual chance and are not flagged, however high it is.
